title: Ligation sequencing gDNA-Native Barcoding
purpose: This protocol describes a standardized workflow for preparing genomic DNA (gDNA) libraries for sequencing using the Oxford Nanopore Technologies Ligation Sequencing gDNA Native Barcoding V14 Kit (SQK-NBD114-24 or SQK-NBD114.96). It aims to ensure consistent and reliable library preparation and sequencing results.
scope: This protocol covers gDNA QC, shearing, library preparation including DNA repair and end preparation, native barcode ligation, sample pooling, sequencing adapter ligation, and final library preparation. It also includes loading the prepared library onto a compatible Oxford Nanopore sequencing flow cell and initiating a sequencing run. The procedure applies to trained laboratory personnel performing gDNA library preparation and sequencing using this kit.

steps: Quantify samples following the standard Qubit procedure using the Qubit dsDNA HS reagent kit and record your concentration values in ng/µL.
Check the integrity of DNA on the Agilent TapeStation using the Agilent TapeStation gDNA reagents kit and record your DIN.
Analyze the combined metrics using the following criteria to determine how to proceed:

rows: 600 ng if multiplexing more than four samples. 1.2 µg if multiplexing less than four samples.
**Low concentration:** Re-extract the sample or concentrate if in high volume.
**DNA Integrity Number (DIN) 7.0** and standard sizing peak **> 40 kb**.
**Degraded Sample (DIN < 6.0, sizing < 40 kb):** Skip the Covaris fragmentation step entirely. Proceed directly to end-repair, or re-extract the sample.

steps.title: DNA Fragmentation via Covaris Mechanical Shearing
steps.intro: The purpose of this step is to mechanically shear high-molecular-weight, intact genomic DNA (gDNA) into a uniform, targeted fragment size distribution (typically **8 kb to 15 kb** for standard long-read ligation workflows).

equipment: Calibrated benchtop centrifuge capable of generating specific RPMs (if using g-TUBEs)

steps: Based on the concentration determined by the Qubit in Step 1, calculate the volume of gDNA required to meet the input threshold (600 ng).
Dilute with nuclease-free water to a total volume of 150 µL. See table below.
Note your specific microcentrifuge model and cross-reference your total DNA mass with your targeted fragment size to determine your required RPM (Tables 1 and 2).

steps.caption: Recommended centrifugation speed (RPM) for different input mass and the targeted DNA fragment size for Eppendorf® 5424 and 5415 R (24-position rotor)
Recommended centrifugation speed (RPM) for different input mass and the targeted DNA fragment size for Eppendorf® MiniSpin plus

steps.text: Microcentrifuge acceleration must never exceed 16,000 x g (RCF).

steps: Place a new g-TUBE into the LOAD position of the prep station stand with the blue screw-cap facing up.
Unscrew and remove the blue cap.
Pipette exactly 150 µL of your diluted DNA sample directly into the top chamber of the tube. Make sure your sample is free from particulate matter and DNA is fully dissolved.

steps.text: Close the g-TUBE. Screw the blue cap on very firmly by hand.
substeps: If additional leverage is required, insert the tube vertically into the prep stand slot and use the stand as a wrench to tighten the cap firmly.

steps: Proceed to the centrifugation stage **within 15 minutes of loading**.
Insert the g-TUBE into the microcentrifuge rotor with the screw-cap facing UP. Ensure the rotor is properly balanced with an extra g-TUBE if necessary.
Input the selected RPM and processing time determined in Section A, step 3.
Initiate the spin cycle.
Remove the g-TUBE and perform a visual check. The entire sample liquid volume must have drained completely from the upper chamber to the bottom.
Invert the g-TUBE so that the screw-cap is now facing DOWN.
Place the inverted tube back into the centrifuge rotor.
Spin the sample a second time using the exact same speed and time duration used in the first pass.
Proceed to sample collection within 15 minutes of completion.
Remove the g-TUBE from the rotor, keeping the screw-cap facing down at all times.
Seat the inverted tube securely into the UNLOAD position of the prep station stand.
Gently unscrew the clear tube body from the top, leaving the blue screw-cap (which now holds the sheared liquid sample) resting in the stand slot.
Pipette your sheared DNA from inside the cap using a standard pipette tip. Tilting the prep stand slightly can optimize sample visibility and recovery volume.
Proceed to the next step.

issues.problem: Sample liquid is stuck in the upper chamber after the first pass
issues.cause: Minor particulate matter or high-density impurities are blocking the internal ruby orifice.
action: Repeat the first spin pass (screw-cap up) at the configured speed until all fluid clears into the bottom chamber.
If the block persists, invert the tube (screw-cap down) and spin at 4,300 x g (RCF) for 30 seconds to force the sample backward into the cap.
Recover the sample from the cap, pass the liquid through a 0.45 µm filtration device (e.g., Millipore Millex 4 mm filter), and clean the solution before re-trying with a brand-new g-TUBE.

issues.problem: Low recovery volume / fluid sweated into screw threads
issues.cause: The blue cap was not screwed on tightly enough before spinning, allowing fluid to travel into the threads.
issues.action: The sample is not lost. Pipette out whatever fluid is in the cap reservoir first. Re-assemble the tube body onto the cap tightly, invert it (cap down), and run a brief pulse-spin at low RPM for a few seconds. Re-open the tube in the unload stand to recover the remaining trapped fluid from the cap.

issues.problem: Sheared DNA size is smaller than target expectation
issues.cause: Degradation of the input material or an initial gDNA length under 45 kbp.
issues.action: Assess your raw material quality via gel electrophoresis or TapeStation. If your input gDNA yields a smeared profile, decrease your centrifuge RPM parameters on subsequent runs to offset the lower starting size.

substeps: Transfer each sample into a clean 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube.

steps.title: Native Barcode Ligation and Clean-up
steps.intro: To attach a unique native barcode to each DNA sample, allowing multiple samples to be combined and sequenced on one flow cell.

consumables: 0.2 mL PCR tubes or PCR plate

steps: Aliquot 10 µL of NEB Blunt/TA Ligase Master Mix into a clean PCR plate or strip in the master mix area.
Add 7.5 µL of end-prepped DNA sample into each sample well in the pre-PCR area.
Add 2.5 µL of the assigned Native Barcode to each sample.
Mix by pipetting 10 to 20 times between additions.
Gently pipette the reaction to ensure thorough mixing and briefly centrifuge the tubes.
Incubate the reaction in a thermal cycler for **20 minutes at 20 °C.**
Add 4 µL of EDTA (blue cap) to each reaction, mix thoroughly by pipetting and briefly centrifuge.
Pool **all** the barcoded reactions into a clean 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube.
Resuspend the AMPure XP beads thoroughly by vortexing.

steps.text: Add a 0.4x ratio of AMPure XP beads to the pooled reaction and mix well by pipetting. The required volume recommended when using the EDTA blue cap is:

steps: Incubate on a Hula mixer for 10 minutes at room temperature. If a Hula mixer is absent, gently flick the tube every 2 minutes.
Pulse spin and place the tube on a magnetic rack for approximately 5 minutes, or until the supernatant is clear.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Add **700 µL of Short Fragment Buffer** to the bead pellet.
Gently flick the tube to resuspend the beads, briefly centrifuge, and return the tube to the magnetic rack.
Allow the beads to collect and remove the supernatant.
Repeat the Short Fragment Buffer wash using another 700 µL.
Briefly centrifuge and return the tube to the magnetic rack.
Carefully remove any residual buffer.
Remove the tube from the rack and resuspend the beads in 35 µL of nuclease-free water by gently flicking.
Incubate at 37°C for 10 minutes. Every 2 minutes, gently flick the tube for approximately 10 seconds to aid DNA elution.
Place the tube on the magnetic rack until the eluate is clear.
Transfer 32 µL of the eluate into a clean 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube.
Quantify 1 µL of the purified barcoded library using a Qubit fluorometer.
Proceed to the adapter ligation stage.

content.text: The purified barcoded DNA may be stored at 4°C overnight.

steps: Add **20 µL AMPure XP beads** (supplied with ONT kit) to the sample tube. Pipette up and down and pulse centrifuge to collect all liquid at the bottom of the tube.
Incubate on a Hula mixer (rotator mixer) for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Pulse spin the sample ("on-off") to collect all liquid at the bottom of the tube. **Do not pellet the beads.**
Place the tube on a magnetic rack and incubate for 5 mins or until the beads have pelleted and the supernatant is completely clear.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant, being careful not to touch the bead pellet.
Remove the tube from the magnet and wash the beads by adding 125 µL Short Fragment Buffer or Long Fragment Buffer.
Pipette up and down to resuspend and pulse spin ("on-off"). **Do not pellet the beads.**
Place the tube back on the magnetic rack and allow the beads to pellet.
Remove the supernatant using a pipette and discard.
Repeat steps 6 to 9 for a total of two washes.
Resuspend the pellet in 17 µL Elution Buffer and pipette up and down to mix.
Pulse spin ("on-off"). **Do not pellet the beads.**
Incubate for 10 minutes at 37°C. Every 2 minutes, agitate the sample by gently flicking for 10 seconds to encourage DNA elution.
Pellet the beads on a magnet until the eluate is clear and colourless, for at least 2 minutes.
Remove and retain 15 µL of eluate containing the DNA library in a clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf DNA LoBind tube.
Quantify 1 µL of eluted sample using the Qubit HS dsDNA assay on the Qubit fluorometer.

content.text: The final library can now be stored at 4 °C for up to a week or at -80°C for up to 3 months if needed; otherwise proceed directly to MinION sequencing. Keep the prepared library on ice or at 4°C until it is ready to be loaded.

content.label: Safe stopping point and storage
items: Single use or long-term storage exceeding three months: -80°C in DNA LoBind tubes.

steps.title: Sequencing
steps.intro: This step outlines the steps involved in sequencing on either the MinION or GridION.

content.title: Flow Cell Priming
content.intro: Prepare the flow cell for sequencing.

steps: Refer to ONT documentation for images explaining how to check, prime, and load the flow cell.
Complete a flow cell check: open the MinKNOW user interface and load the flow cell onto the MinION. Press down firmly on the flow cell to ensure correct thermal and electrical contact.
Click Flow Cell Check in the MinKNOW interface.
To prepare the flow cell priming mix, combine the following reagents in the FCF tube and mix by inverting the tube and pipette mixing at room temperature.
Slide the flow cell priming port cover clockwise to open the priming port.

After opening the priming port, set a P1000 pipette to 200 µL, insert the tip into the priming port, and turn the wheel until the dial shows 220 to 230 µL, to draw back 20 to 30 µL or until you can see a small volume of buffer entering the pipette tip.
Visually check that there is continuous buffer from the priming port across the sensor array.
Load 800 µL of the priming mix into the flow cell via the priming port, avoiding the introduction of air bubbles.
**Wait for five minutes.** During this time, prepare the library for loading by following the steps below.

steps: Dilute the library in 12 µL of Elution Buffer, using the recommended loading quantity for the fragment size as shown in the table below.

In a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf DNA LoBind tube, prepare the library for loading as follows. Do not mix at this point.

steps.text: Load the library onto the flow cell immediately after adding SB and LIB, because the fuel in the buffer will start to be consumed by the adapter.

steps: Complete flow cell priming: lift the SpotON sample port cover and load 200 µL of the remaining priming mix into the flow cell priming port (not the SpotON sample port), avoiding the introduction of air bubbles.
Mix the prepared library gently by pipetting a few times just prior to loading.

Add half of the library (~37.5 µL) to the flow cell via the SpotON sample port in a dropwise fashion. Ensure each drop flows into the port before adding the next. Resuspend the beads/library and add the second half in a dropwise fashion.
Gently replace the SpotON sample port cover, making sure the bung enters the SpotON port, and close the priming port.
Place the light shield onto the flow cell and close the device lid.

content.title: Pausing or Stopping the Sequencing Run

steps: Open MinKNOW.
Pause the run if reloading, or stop the sequencing experiment if sufficient data has been generated.
Confirm that the flow cell is no longer actively sequencing.
Leave the flow cell inserted in the MinION or GridION device throughout the washing procedure.
The flow cell light shield may remain in place during washing. If it is removed to improve visibility, ensure that it is replaced before sequencing resumes or a new run begins.
Ensure that the priming port cover is closed.
Ensure that the SpotON sample port cover is closed.
Confirm that both covers are properly positioned.

content.text: Keeping these ports closed while removing the waste buffer helps prevent air from being drawn across the sensor array, which can cause substantial loss of sequencing channels.

steps: Set the P1000 micropipette to 1,000 µL.
Fit the pipette with an appropriate tip.
Insert the tip into waste port 1.
Slowly aspirate the waste buffer from the waste channel.
Continue until the waste buffer has been removed.
If necessary, dispense the aspirated liquid into an appropriate waste receptacle and repeat the aspiration until the waste channel has been emptied.
Keep the priming port and SpotON sample port closed throughout this operation.

steps.text: Perform the aspiration slowly. With the priming and SpotON ports closed, fluid should not leave the sensor array.

steps: Proceed to the wash step after the waste buffer has been removed.
Locate the flow cell priming port.
Slide the priming port cover clockwise to open it.
Inspect the area beneath the cover for a small air bubble.
Set the P1000 micropipette to 200 µL.
Insert the pipette tip into the priming port.
Carefully draw back a small amount of liquid. The manufacturer's instructions describe adjusting the pipette dial to approximately 220 to 230 µL to withdraw a small volume.
Inspect the flow cell visually.
Confirm that a continuous layer of buffer remains between the priming port and the sensor array.

content.label: Precaution
content.text: Do not withdraw more than 20 to 30 µL from the flow cell during this operation. The nanopore array must remain covered by buffer at all times. Introducing air bubbles into the array can irreversibly damage pores.

steps: Using a P1000 micropipette, take 200 µL of the flow cell wash mix.
Inspect the pipette tip and ensure that it contains no air bubbles.
Insert the tip into the priming port.
Dispense the wash mixture slowly and continuously.
If the pipette permits, use its wheel to control the dispensing rate. Otherwise, depress the plunger very slowly.
Avoid introducing air into the flow cell.
Start a timer immediately after loading the first 200 µL.
Allow the wash mixture to remain in the flow cell for 5 minutes.
After the 5-minute incubation, take the remaining 200 µL of the prepared wash mixture.
Load the second 200 µL through the priming port using the same slow, continuous dispensing technique.
Close the priming port cover.
Allow the wash mixture to incubate for 1 hour.

content.title: Remove the Waste Buffer After Washing

substeps: Keep the priming port and SpotON sample port closed.
Set the P1000 micropipette to 1,000 µL.
Insert the pipette tip into waste port 1.
Slowly aspirate the waste buffer.
Repeat the aspiration if necessary, until all waste buffer has been removed from the waste channel.

steps: Proceed immediately to either preparation for loading a subsequent sequencing library (Option A) or preparation of the flow cell for storage (Option B).

content.title: Post-wash Option A: Preparation for Another Sequencing Run
content.intro: If the flow cell will be reused immediately, follow the protocol for priming and loading the sequencing library.

content.title: Post-wash Option B: Storing the Flow Cell

steps: Allow one tube of Storage Buffer (S) to thaw at room temperature.
Slide the flow cell priming port cover clockwise to open it.
Inspect the area beneath the cover for a small air bubble.
If necessary, carefully draw back a small amount of liquid using the manufacturer's specified priming-port procedure.
Do not withdraw more than 20 to 30 µL, and ensure that the nanopore array remains covered by buffer.
Using a P1000 micropipette, take 500 µL of Storage Buffer (S).
Insert the tip into the priming port.
Slowly dispense the Storage Buffer into the flow cell.
Close the priming port.
Set the P1000 micropipette to 1,000 µL.
Insert the pipette tip into waste port 1.
Slowly aspirate the waste buffer from the waste channel.
Repeat the aspiration if necessary, until the waste channel has been emptied.
Store the flow cell at 2 to 8°C.

items: After washing or storage, perform a flow cell check to determine the number of nanopores available for another sequencing run.
When the flow cell is required again, remove it from storage and allow it to warm to room temperature for approximately 5 minutes before proceeding with the appropriate reuse workflow.
